original_question: Fix k >= 1 and N. For the space F_N^(k) of symmetric superpolynomials in N even variables and N odd variables that vanish whenever x_1 = x_2 = ... = x_{k+1}, do the Jack superpolynomials P^(alpha_{k,2})_Lambda(x_1, ..., x_N, theta_1, ..., theta_N) indexed by (k, 2, N)-admissible superpartitions form a basis of F_N^(k)?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in the introduction, with Proposition 1.2 giving the equivalent equality-of-spaces reformulation and Theorem 1.3 providing the proved inclusion that motivates the conjecture.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly singles out the r = 2 case, the space F_N^(k) defined by the k-clustering vanishing condition, the Jack superpolynomials P_Λ^(α_(k,2)) at the negative fractional parameter α_(k,2), the indexing by (k,2,N)-admissible superpartitions, and the basis question itself. That is essentially the content of the paper’s Conjecture 1.1.
missing_details: The ambient space should be specified as symmetric superpolynomials in N commuting variables x_1,…,x_N and N anticommuting variables θ_1,…,θ_N, with θ_iθ_j = -θ_jθ_i and θ_i^2 = 0.
Symmetry should be stated as invariance under the diagonal action of S_N simultaneously permuting the x-variables and the θ-variables.
The parameter should be written explicitly as α_(k,2) = -(k+1) (since α_(k,r) = -(k+1)/(r-1) and here r = 2).

The admissibility condition should be defined explicitly, not just named: for a superpartition Λ of length at most N, (k,2,N)-admissibility is expressed in terms of Λ^* and Λ^∘* (or Λ* and Λ⊛, depending on notation) by the paper’s inequality Λ_i^∘* - Λ_(i+k)^* ≥ 2 for all relevant i.

The question is graded across all bosonic and fermionic degrees, so if one wants a stand-alone formulation one should say that these Jack superpolynomials form a graded basis, equivalently a basis degree-by-degree.

The space F_N^(k) should be defined as a subspace of symmetric superpolynomials, and the vanishing condition should be interpreted as setting k+1 commuting variables equal while leaving the odd variables present; by symmetry it suffices to write x_1 = ⋯ = x_(k+1).
To match the paper’s setup, it is helpful to name I_N^(k,2), the span of the admissible Jack superpolynomials at α_(k,2), because Proposition 1.2 reformulates the conjecture as I_N^(k,2) = F_N^(k).
The well-definedness/regularity of P_Λ^(α_(k,2)) for admissible Λ is implicit in your draft but should be understood as part of the paper’s setup.
refined_question: Fix integers k ≥ 1 and N ≥ 1. Let Λ_N^θ be the ℂ-vector space of polynomials in commuting variables x_1,…,x_N and anticommuting variables θ_1,…,θ_N, invariant under the diagonal action of S_N, and let F_N^(k) ⊂ Λ_N^θ be the subspace of symmetric superpolynomials f such that f(x,θ)|_(x_1=⋯=x_(k+1)) = 0. Write α_(k,2) = -(k+1), and let P_Λ^(α_(k,2))(x_1,…,x_N,θ_1,…,θ_N) denote the Jack superpolynomial indexed by a superpartition Λ with ℓ(Λ) ≤ N that is (k,2,N)-admissible in the sense of the paper. Do the Jack superpolynomials P_Λ^(α_(k,2)) indexed by all (k,2,N)-admissible superpartitions form a graded basis of F_N^(k)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if I_N^(k,2) denotes the span of the Jack superpolynomials P_Λ^(α_(k,2)) indexed by (k,2,N)-admissible superpartitions, is I_N^(k,2) = F_N^(k)?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s precise r = 2 clustering open problem, not a broader question. Conjecture 1.1 asks whether the admissible Jack superpolynomials at α_(k,2) give a basis for the space F_N^(k) of symmetric superpolynomials vanishing when k+1 commuting variables coincide. Proposition 1.2 reformulates this as the equality I_N^(k,2) = F_N^(k). Theorem 1.3 provides the proved half of this statement by showing the admissible Jack superpolynomials satisfy the required clustering vanishing condition, hence span a subspace of F_N^(k). So your draft already identifies the right conjecture, but it needs the full superspace setup, the exact admissibility condition, the explicit parameter value, and the graded/equality-of-spaces formulation to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful.
